building resilience in the face of potential market manipulation. USA Rare Earth, another recipient of US government investment, has acquired a samarium production chain which relies on a British factory and a French stockpile with enough supply for between one and three years of US defense industry consumption. These types of industrial partnerships with Europe can fill American critical gaps. What Europe lacks in scale and investment, it makes up for in specialized expertise which is difficult, expensive, and time-consuming to replicate. Solvay, USA Rare Earth’s partner, has both a stockpile and rare-earth know-how. Its plant at La Rochelle, France, has been processing rare earths since 1948. Less Common Metals, a British metal and alloy producer, is now owned by USA Rare Earth and has a proprietary SmCo magnet production process that rivals China’s. Other German, Finnish, Swedish, and Estonian firms also have current or planned capacities across the rare earth permanent magnet supply chain—ranging from upstream mining and separation to SmCo magnet production. The European Union’s vast market offers a strong demand base for the expanding Western critical minerals production. Since adopting the Critical Raw Materials Act in 2024, the bloc has built a regulatory and policy framework for both internal investment and multilateral cooperation. The European Commission plans to establish a European Critical Raw Materials Center, designed to coordinate demand aggregation and project financing for minerals by drawing on some of the continent’s comparative strengths: market intelligence and cross-country coordination. The Center could provide a critical channel for information sharing and stakeholder mapping for US firms. This year, Washington and Brussels agreed to discuss border-adjusted price floors and offtake agreements. In addition, there are national initiatives; German companies, including BMW and Rheinmetall, said on November 23 that they planned a trading house to secure critical minerals. Europe is also widening its supplier base, and two partnerships stand out. The EU and Canada are pursuing multiple streams for critical mineral industry partnership, including closer cooperation on stockpiling and batteries, while in the longer run, the bloc’s relationship with Ukraine offers downstream demand. In July, the EU launched a defense industrial partnership with Kyiv covering drones, missile defense, artillery and other key components. Ukraine, which already mines titanium ore, has a critical minerals strategy and action plan and is actively seeking partners. No individual country has the scale or financing capability to build a fully self-reliant minerals supply chain to offset potential Chinese market manipulation. And time is short: China already dominates and has shown it is willing to restrict supplies, as it did to Japan in 2010 and to the US in 2025 , and has undercut competitors on price. Twelve NATO allies took an important step at this year’s NATO Ankara summit by formally launching a joint defense-critical raw materials initiative. The US, which is not a participant, should embrace this initiative and work with its allies to complement strategic reserves with long-term purchasing commitments and coordinated industrial investment. The immediate challenge is not to eliminate every dependency on China, but to ensure Beijing cannot interrupt essential Western defense production. The US should embrace Europe’s existing critical minerals capabilities as strategic assets, not simply temporary substitutes until American production comes online. Partnership on critical mineral supply chains both increases transatlantic security and serves as a nexus of transatlantic market growth and expertise-sharing that could move from catch-up to innovation and true resiliency. The goal should be to build a competitive allied industrial ecosystem that China cannot easily disrupt. Sharon Hudson-Dean is a Senior Fellow at the Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA) and an Associate Fellow at Chatham House in London. She is a veteran diplomat and senior foreign policy leader who has managed complex strategic, defense, and political policies throughout her career. Most recently, she served as US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for Northern Europe, NATO, and Arctic Security (2024-25). Anping Zhu is a Yale University student majoring in global affairs, economics, and mathematics. He is a research assistant to CEPA Fellow Sharon Hudson-Dean for her expert comment series on critical minerals and the race to secure Western supply. He is a member of the Yale Foreign Policy Initiative and has worked as a policy research intern and adviser to the governments of Lesotho and Rwanda. 摘要：台湾 11 月 28 日的地方选举重点关注民生问题，包括交通、住房负担能力、基础设施和社会福利。他们还将塑造 2028 年总统选举之前的政治格局。结果将反映选民对赖清德总统领导下的现任民进党政府的满意度。强劲的表现将表明该党能够在台湾南部的传统据点之外维持支持。国民党目前占据 22 个最高行政职位中的 16 个。台北、新北和台中的关键选举结果将影响2028年的候选人名单，其中包括现任台中市长卢秀妍和台北市长蒋万安。台湾人民党 (TPP) 正在合作推翻民进党候选人，不过结果将决定这种合作是否持续到 2028 年。北京的干预并不是这次选举的主要话题，但它提供了竞选资金，创建了机器人账户来影响媒体叙事，并对与民进党结盟的个人进行跨国镇压。台湾将于11月28日举行四年来首次地方选举。
近2000万符合资格的成年人（20岁或以上）将投票选出从市长、县长到当地村长的九个职位的代表，因此俗称“九合一选举”。地方选举通常关注基础设施发展和电价等民生问题。今年也不例外，候选人强调解决生活成本和生活质量问题的政策。台湾的党派政治不太关注意识形态，而是关注实际问题和政治人物，因此候选人的日常媒体露面和政策辩论在选民心目中的影响力更大。房间里的大象是迫在眉睫的总统选举，定于 2028 年初举行，九合一选举将有助于奠定基础。这是因为，无论哪个政党在 11 月份脱颖而出，都将为在地方一级获得多数席位的政党提供动力，而且地方政治也为通往国家办公室提供了共同的垫脚石。该国的集权化，加上其规模较小，为市长——特别是直辖市的市长——提供了一条相当直接的通往国家级权力的道路。其强大的媒体环境，对地方政客的频繁报道，也支持了他们的崛起。
民生问题候选人竞选进入本周期，国民党占据了22个地方高级行政职位中的16个。这使其有些脆弱，因为它有更多席位可以失去，包括新北、台中和彰化等摇摆城市和县。而民进党则拥有五个辖区，均位于传统据点南方。尽管民进党可能会获得更多好处，但其最近在地方选举中的记录值得警惕。该党在2018年惨败，2022年再次表现不佳，导致台湾前总统蔡英文辞去党主席职务（台湾电视台[台视]，2022年11月26日）。金门县是唯一的另一个县，由曾短暂加入台湾人民党（TPP）的无党派人士控制。对于第三

Executive Summary: Taiwan’s local elections on November 28 are focused on bread-and-butter issues, including transportation, housing affordability, infrastructure, and social welfare. They will also shape the political landscape leading up to the 2028 presidential elections. Results will reflect voter satisfaction with the incumbent Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) administration under President Lai Ching-te. A strong showing will be a sign that the party is able to maintain support beyond its traditional stronghold in Southern Taiwan. The Kuomintang (KMT) currently holds 16 of the 22 top executive posts. Outcomes of key races in Taipei, New Taipei, and Taichung will affect its pool of candidates for 2028, including current Taichung mayor Lu Shiow-yen and Taipei mayor Chiang Wan-an. The Taiwan People’s Party (TPP) is cooperating to unseat DPP candidates, though results will determine whether that cooperation continues through to 2028. Beijing’s interference is not a major talking point in this election, but it has provided campaign funds, created bot accounts to influence media narratives, and engaged in transnational repression against individuals aligned with the DPP. Taiwan is set to hold local elections for the first time in four years on November 28. Nearly 20 million eligible adults (those aged 20 or older) will vote for representatives in nine positions ranging from city mayors and county magistrates down to local village chiefs—hence the colloquial name the “nine-in-one elections” (九合一選舉). Local elections typically focus on bread-and-butter issues such as infrastructure development and electricity prices. This year is no different, with candidates emphasizing policies to tackle cost-of-living and quality-of-life concerns. Partisan politics in Taiwan is less focused on ideology than on practical issues and political personalities, and so candidates’ day-to-day media appearances and policy debates carry more weight in the minds of voters. The elephant in the room is the looming presidential election, scheduled for early 2028, for which the nine-in-one elections will help set the stage. This is because candidates who come out on top in November will provide momentum for whichever party manages to secure a majority at the local level, and because local politics also provides a common stepping stone to national office. The country’s centralization, coupled with its small size, provides mayors—specifically those of special municipalities (直轄市)—a fairly direct path to national-level prominence. Its robust media environment, which provides frequent coverage of local-level politicians, also supports their ascendance. Candidates Campaign on Bread-and-Butter Issues Going into this cycle, the Kuomintang (KMT) holds 16 of 22 top local executive posts. This makes it somewhat vulnerable, as it has more seats to lose, including swing cities and counties such as New Taipei, Taichung, and Changhua. The Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), meanwhile, holds five jurisdictions, all of which are located in the South, a traditional stronghold. Although the DPP might have more to gain, its recent record in local elections is a cautionary one. The party suffered a heavy defeat in 2018 and another poor showing in 2022 led to former Taiwan president Tsai Ing-wen (蔡英文) resigning as party chair ( Taiwan Television [TTV] , November 26, 2022). Kinmen, the only other county, is held by an independent that briefly joined the Taiwan People’s Party (TPP). For these elections, the TPP has decided to cooperate with the KMT in a “blue-white coalition” (藍白合), and is contesting only the Chiayi County magistrate election. Local campaigns tend to focus on the day-to-day issues that fall within the purview of local governments, such as urban renewal and transportation development. Housing affordability is a major issue in Taiwan, especially in the north, and some candidates have unveiled plans to construct more public housing, with priority given to young people who do not own property ( United Daily News [UDN] , November 20). Others are promising new transportation infrastructure. In New Taipei, for instance, KMT candidate Lee Shu-chuan (李四川) has proposed a metro line crossing the Dahan River and light-rail connections linking Linkou, Bali, and Tamsui with the nearby Taoyuan Metro network ( Mirror Media , July 31). In Taichung, KMT candidate Johnny Chiang (江啟臣), who is currently deputy speaker of the Legislative Yuan, is proposing a “20-minute city” (20分鐘生活圈) in which residents can access essential services close to home. His opponent, DPP legislator Ho Hsin-chun (何欣純), is running on a platform to reduce traffic congestion and make improvements to the city’s transportation system ( UDN , September 15; Ho Hsin-chun Campaign Office , accessed November 12). Demographic challenges are also prominent. Taiwan has had declining birth rates and an aging population since the 2010s, but people are only now starting to feel the economic impact of these changes. As municipal governments are responsible for much of the service delivery for social welfare, candidates are responding to a growing demand for childcare, maternal health services, hospice care, and migrant caregiver policies. These issues are particularly relevant to younger voters, who face rising housing costs and the financial burden of supporting older family members ( Now News , November 23). Alongside the nine-in-one elections, voters are asked to decide on specific national issues at the polls. Unusually, the franchise is expanded for these referenda to those aged 18 and 19. This year, the issue on the ballot is whether to use nuclear power to revitalize the economy, overturning the Tsai Ing-wen government’s “nuclear-free homeland” (非核家園) policy. Nuclear energy has been a topic of perennial political contestation in Taiwan. The latest referendum—the fourth on the issue since 2018—comes on the heels of Taiwan becoming “nuclear-free” in 2025, when its last reactor reached the end of its 40-year lifespan ( China Brief , August 23, 2024; Taiwan Central News Agency [CNA] , November 12). President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) has previously indicated openness to restarting nuclear energy production, saying that he “does not wish to exclude any particular energy source due to ideology” (不要因為意識形態，而排除任何一種能源) ( UDN , October 16). Elections to set Stage for 2028 The upcoming election will likely have a significant impact on how parties approach 2028. This is particularly true for the KMT, who will use the vote to assess candidates’ viability for the country’s highest office. Lai will likely attempt to seek a second term for the DPP, while the TPP will have choices to make depending on both its own performance and that of the KMT. The six special municipalities (直轄市)—Taipei, New Taipei, Taoyuan, Taichung, Tainan, and Kaohsiung—are politically the most consequential. These cities account for the majority of the population and of economic activity on the island, and their mayors have greater national visibility than other local officials. Among these, the Taipei mayor is the most prominent. Three of five previous presidents had previously served in this role, while others have gone on to chair their respective political parties ( GTI , October 30). Some see the KMT incumbent, Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安), as a torchbearer for a younger KMT, and pundits—including former 2024 vice presidential candidate Jaw Shaw-kong (趙少康)—have speculated about a 2028 presidential run ( TTV News , October 20). But even though Taipei is traditionally a stronghold for the KMT, Chiang has seen his polling numbers slip to an innovative campaign by DPP challenger Shen Pao-yang (沈伯洋; a.k.a. Puma Shen). Shen, whose campaign is colloquially called “ocean current” (洋流), punning on a homophone of his name, has overcome a more than 20-point deficit over the last six months, making the race too close to call ( SET News , May 7; TVBS , May 27; Initium Media , November 17).  [1] His popularity has even led other DPP candidates to vie for joint appearances, in the hope of boosting their own chances ( Liberty Times [LTN] , November 23). Taichung will be a key bellwether for the KMT, where incumbent mayor Lu Shiow-yen (盧秀燕) has reached the end of her second term. The party hopes to retain the mayoralty and preserve Lu’s political legacy, as she is widely considered a presidential contender ( Storm Media , September 15). If Johnny Chiang successfully defends the seat, his win would preserve the KMT’s political patronage network in central Taiwan and allow Lu to claim credit for managing the succession and for good governance. Conversely, a DPP victory would weaken her position and damage her chances for a 2028 bid, while potentially strengthening the standing of other figures, such as KMT chairperson Cheng Li-wun (鄭麗文). New Taipei City, the country’s most populous administrative division, is home to four million people, making it a key battleground. The DPP last governed the city in 2005, under Su Tseng-chang (蘇貞昌), who later served as premier in both the Chen Shui-bian (陳水扁) and Tsai Ing-wen administrations. His daughter, Su Chiao-hui (蘇巧慧), is running as the DPP candidate against KMT candidate Lee Shu-chuan. Su Chiao-hui has touted her experience as a sitting legislator and announced family-oriented neonatal and hospice care policies, while Lee, drawing on his technocratic background as a civil engineer and his long stints as deputy mayor of Taipei, New Taipei, and Kaohsiung, has focused on urban renewal projects ( CNA , August 19; Su Chiao-hui New Taipei City Mayoral Campaign Office , accessed November 10). Polling numbers indicate both candidates are within a few percentage points of each other and the race has been described as a toss-up ( Legislator Lin Chu-yin , November 13; TTV , November 16). A DPP win would likely shock the KMT, and improve the party’s assessments of its chances for 2028. In Kaohsiung, a southern port metropolis of 2.5 million people, both candidates are sitting legislators. In the campaign, the DPP’s Lai Jui-lung (賴瑞隆) has attacked the KMT’s Ko Chi-en (柯志恩) and her party’s legislative caucus for passing amendments to the revenue allocation law, which controls how much funding municipalities receive from the central government. Kaohsiung was one of the losers after the reallocation, leading to accusations from the pan-Green camp that the amendments are the latest manifestation of the sentiment that resources and capital often “prioritize the North at the expense of the South” (重北輕南) in Taiwan ( FTV News , August 29).  [2] The Kaohsiung City Government has argued that the city needs more funds because it is in the midst of industrial upgrading and that it has borne the brunt of environmental pollution arising from its massive industrial economy ( Kaohsiung City Government , December 21, 2024). Current polling indicates a DPP win is likely in Kaohsiung ( Radio Taiwan International , November 16). Outside of the special municipalities, Changhua stands out as the most crucial race. The largest county by population, it is home to 1.25 million people. The primary process for selecting candidates was marred by controversy, mainly arising from factional politics. The KMT candidate, Wei Cheng-ping (魏政平), does not come from the factions system and is seen as a compromise, which has led to local resentment against Cheng Li-wun’s electoral strategy (Cheng is personally acting as the head of Wei’s campaign) ( UDN , October 13). The DPP candidate, Chen Su-yueh (陳素月), has the backing of some local factions, but faces a split pan-Green ticket. DPP Changhua County Party Chapter chair Chiu Chien-fu (邱建富) is also running, but as an independent. Polls have Chen in the lead, but 40 percent of Changhua voters are still undecided ( CNA ; UDN , October 19). (Source: Author research) At the national level, the DPP’s primary concern is whether it can maintain its electoral coalition after holding the presidency for three consecutive terms. Lai’s 2024 victory, with 40 percent of the popular vote, fell short of a majority. The ensuing lack of control over the legislature has rendered him unable to effectively enact his agenda. Partisan fights over the central budget, defense, and legislative power have resulted in legislative gridlock throughout much of 2025 and 2026. When coupled with the failure of a set of recall campaigns to remove KMT legislators in mid-2025, the party’s legitimacy may have suffered in the eyes of voters ( China Brief , July 7, 2025). A strong DPP showing in northern and central Taiwan would show that the party can maintain support beyond its traditional southern strongholds. Optimistic projections for the DPP describe the party as “sitting on three, looking at four, and gazing at five” (坐三望四看五) of the six special municipalities. This refers to the party having a good chance of taking Tainan, Kaohsiung, and New Taipei, an even chance of taking Taipei, and an outside chance in Taichung ( LTN , November 12). Conversely, a poor performance could reinforce perceptions of public dissatisfaction with the administration and may spell trouble for Lai’s reelection bid. The elections may help clarify the TPP’s future, too. In 2024, presidential candidate Ko Wen-je (柯文哲) received roughly 26 percent of the vote, while his party secured just over 22 percent of the party-list vote. The TPP has struggled with an identity crisis since then, however, and under the leadership of chairperson Huang Kuo-chang (黃國昌) has closely aligned itself with KMT legislative priorities and pursued a confrontational approach with the DPP. Its decision to cooperate with the KMT in the 2026 local elections may be a marriage of convenience where both opposition parties coordinate to improve their chances of defeating DPP candidates. A strong KMT performance could encourage the two opposition parties to pursue another joint presidential ticket in 2028, though the coalition is already fraying in some places, raising the chances that they will fail to coordinate effectively, just as happened in 2024 ( CNA , September 9). Two alternative options involve the TPP either concluding that its independent electoral base remains sufficiently large to justify fielding its own candidate, or deciding to enter a quid-pro-quo arrangement where it runs a joint ticket with the KMT in exchange for political or legislative concessions. Persistent PRC Pressure Through Interference and Transnational Repression Cross-Strait relations are not a priority issue for this election, but attempts by the People’s Republic of China (PRC) to interfere, including through ongoing acts of transnational repression, loom large over the election. Candidates have had different reasons for avoiding the issue. DPP candidates may be downplaying the issue to shake the label that the party simply campaigns on the platform of “protecting Taiwan through opposing the PRC” (抗中保台). KMT and TPP candidates, conversely, may avoid the subject because PRC electoral interference efforts often benefit their candidates. For instance, a TPP candidate for Taoyuan City councilor, Chou Hsiao-yun (周曉芸), was recently indicted for allegedly taking campaign funds from Chinese Communist Party (CCP) officials and collecting photos of Taiwanese citizens for PRC bot farms to deploy to influence electoral narratives ( SET News ; KNews , November 20; Taipei Times , November 24). PRC disinformation campaigns appear to have stepped up this year. Taiwan’s National Security Bureau recorded more than 2.5 million instances of misleading online content between January and September, compared to 1.7 million during the same period in 2025. These campaigns have targeted issues such as energy policy, food safety, defense, candidate platforms, and local infrastructure development ( TaiSounds , October 21). The PRC also seems to have escalated its transnational repression to include physical intimidation. Recent cases include an assault on comedian Huang Yi-hao (黃逸豪) that is alleged to have been directed by PRC-based instigators, a smear campaign against entertainment personality Tsai Kang-yong (蔡康永) for attending a Puma Shen rally, and an outstanding arrest warrant and cash bounty against Shen himself. These incidents remind voters that the PRC remains a factor, even in an election mainly fought over domestic priorities ( UDN , October 7; China Brief , November 5).  [3] Conclusion The results of the nine-in-one elections will predominantly reflect voter sentiment on quality-of-life issues and political personalities. They will also provide a temperature check on the Lai administration, and signal whether voters are satisfied after a decade of DPP rule. Shifting political alliances and factional politics will likely dominate the political landscape for the next two years, as parties assess the viability of their potential candidates. The results will also have significant implications for cross-Strait relations. A strong KMT performance could strengthen the party’s argument that Taiwanese voters favor a less confrontational approach to Beijing and improve the political standing of candidates advocating renewed cross-Strait dialogue. A strong DPP performance would instead lend credence to the party’s belief that Taiwanese voters are skeptical of the KMT’s more dovish approach to Beijing. [2] Political parties in Taiwan and their allies are referred to in different colors. The DPP is the Green camp (綠營) or pan-Green camp (泛綠), the KMT is the Blue camp (藍營) or pan-Blue camp (泛藍), and the TPP’s colors are white. [3] The impact of Beijing’s traditional united front activities appears more limited in scope. Twenty-five “Chinese spouses” (中配)—that is, immigrants from the PRC who have acquired Taiwanese citizenship through marriage—registered as candidates in the local elections, with some candidates failing to provide evidence that they have abandoned their PRC citizenship ( LTN , September 8; TaiSounds , October 1). 摘要：在党的二十大上，以前组织部部长陈曦为中心的清华系是习近平周围的权力极之一。随着中央政治局委员陈吉宁被立案调查，清华13名正部级以上官员中，有7人被立案调查、下台或撤职。派系的崩溃是从陈汐的失宠开始的。 6月，习近平破格保留的中央党校校长职务在陈曦任期结束前由蔡奇接任。一个失去支持的派系没有人为其担保，并担任其他人觊觎的职位，从而加速其崩溃。该集团的核心成员陈吉宁被空降到上海，在那里的四年里几乎没有什么表现。对人工智能的大量投资并没有取得重大突破。这使得习近平很容易将他视为五中全会全面从严治党运动的反面典型。 11月24日，新华社发布消息称，中共中央政治局委员、上海市委书记陈吉宁涉嫌严重违纪违法，目前正接受中央纪律检查委员会组织调查（新华社11月24日电）。上海市委当晚表示支持这一决定（上海市人民政府，11月24日）。
陈是继2006年陈良宇之后第四位落马的第20届政治局委员，也是第二位被落马的上海市委书记（中国网，2006年9月25日）。他曾被广泛视为2027年下半年党的第二十一次代表大会政治局常委的竞争者（华尔街日报，11月24日）。同日，原西安市委书记方红卫与陈清华一样，均是清华大学毕业生，被起诉（财新网，2021年11月7日；新华社，11月24日）。陈吉宁的事业与习近平总书记的清华同学陈希密不可分。陈曦留在了大学，并通过共青团和学生事务晋升为校党委书记。 2013年起，主持中组部日常工作，后出任中组部部长（人民网，2017年10月25日；路透社，2022年10月10日）。他以清华为基地，建立了一个高层网络，被称为“清华帮”。 [1] 2023年，本应完全退休的他却破格留任中央党校校长，从而保留了影响力（人民网，2017年10月25日；联合早报，6月5日）。但从那时起，由于一些成员受到控制或调查，该集团逐渐衰落。 6月，陈曦在任期届满前突然交出国家主席职务（《联合早报》6月5日）。
同月，据信与陈曦关系密切的北京政协主席魏小东受到调查（新华社，6 月 6 日；中国主义，6 月 8 日）。陈吉宁的倒台可能标志着清华系的终结。清华派大半出局，陈吉宁的每次升迁，都追随着陈曦的位置。陈吉宁在2006年和2007年担任清华大学副校长和常务副校长时，陈希担任清华大学党委书记。当他直接从清华大学校长那里走出来的时候

Executive Summary: At the 20th Party Congress, the Tsinghua Clique—centered on former Organization Department head Chen Xi—was one of the poles of power around Xi Jinping. With Politburo member Chen Jining now under investigation, seven of the 13 Tsinghua-affiliated officials at full ministerial rank or above have been placed under investigation, stepped down, or been moved out of their posts. The clique’s collapse began with Chen Xi’s fall from favor. In June, the Central Party School presidency, which Xi had kept for him as an exception, went to Cai Qi before Chen Xi’s term was up. A faction that has lost favor has no one to vouch for it and holds posts others covet, accelerating its collapse. Chen Jining, a core member of the clique, was parachuted into Shanghai and had little to show for his four years there. Heavy investment in artificial intelligence produced no major breakthroughs. This made it easy for Xi to discard him as a negative example for the Fifth Plenum’s campaign of full and rigorous Party self-governance. On November 24, Xinhua announced that Politburo member and Shanghai Party Secretary Chen Jining (陈吉宁) is under investigation by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (CCDI) for suspected serious violations of discipline and law ( Xinhua , November 24). Shanghai’s Party committee pledged its support for the decision that evening ( Shanghai Municipal Government , November 24). Chen is the fourth member of the 20th Politburo to fall, and the second Shanghai Party secretary brought down in office, after Chen Liangyu (陈良宇) in 2006 ( China.org.cn , September 25, 2006). He had been widely seen as a contender for the Politburo Standing Committee at the 21st Party Congress in the second half of 2027 ( Wall Street Journal , November 24). The same day, Fang Hongwei (方红卫), a former Party secretary of Xi’an who, like Chen, is a Tsinghua graduate, was indicted ( Caixin , November 7, 2021; Xinhua , November 24). Chen Jining’s career is inseparable from that of Chen Xi (陈希), General Secretary Xi Jinping’s classmate at Tsinghua. Chen Xi stayed on at the university and rose through the Communist Youth League and student affairs to become its Party secretary. From 2013, he ran the Central Organization Department’s day-to-day work, later becoming its head ( People’s Daily Online , October 25, 2017; Reuters , October 10, 2022). With Tsinghua as his base, he built a high-level network known as the “Tsinghua Clique” (清华帮).  [1] In 2023, when he should have fully retired, he was granted an exception to stay on as president of the Central Party School, allowing him to retain his influence ( People’s Daily Online , October 25, 2017; Lianhe Zaobao , June 5). Yet from then on the clique declined, as some of its members were reined in or investigated. In June, Chen Xi abruptly handed over the presidency before his term was up ( Lianhe Zaobao , June 5). That same month, Wei Xiaodong (魏小东), chairman of the Beijing Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) who is believed to have close ties to Chen Xi, was placed under investigation ( Xinhua , June 6; Sinocism , June 8). Chen Jining’s fall likely marks the end of the Tsinghua Clique. Most of the Tsinghua Clique Is Out Each of Chen Jining’s promotions tracked Chen Xi’s position. When Chen Jining became vice president and then executive vice president of Tsinghua in 2006 and 2007, Chen Xi was the university’s Party secretary. When he went straight from Tsinghua president to minister of environmental protection in 2015, and when he became acting mayor of Beijing in 2017, Chen Xi was running the day-to-day work of the Organization Department. In October 2022, Chen Xi personally announced Chen Jining’s appointment as Shanghai Party secretary ( People’s Daily Online , February 27, 2015; Xinhua , October 28, 2022). Around the 20th Party Congress, Tsinghua cadres with ties to Chen Xi held posts in the Organization Department, the Central Party School, and other central bodies, as well as in Shanghai, Beijing, and several other provinces and cities. Counting only those who studied full-time or worked at Tsinghua, 13 officials held full ministerial rank or above after the 20th Party Congress.  [2] Of these, seven are now out (see Table 1). Hu Heping (胡和平) stepped down as minister of culture and tourism at the end of 2023, retaining only his deputy post at the Propaganda Department (Xinhua, December 29, 2023 , October 30 ). Former Organization Department head Li Ganjie (李干杰), a core figure in Chen Xi’s control over personnel, was transferred in April 2025 to the less influential United Front Work Department ( Central News Agency , April 2, 2025). Hubei Party Secretary Wang Menghui (王蒙徽) and Henan Party Secretary Liu Ning (刘宁) were moved to sinecures at the National People’s Congress (NPC) as they neared retirement age, and Hebei Party Secretary Ni Yuefeng (倪岳峰) followed suit well before reaching it (Xinhua, February 25, 2025 , August 28 , November 6 ). In little more than a year, Fang Hongwei, Qin Weizhong (覃伟中), Xia Linmao (夏林茂), and Chen Jining have all been placed under investigation (Xinhua, November 7, 2025 , September 21 , October 22 ). Everyone Kicks a Faction When It Is Down The two most important posts Chen Xi’s network lost have gone to others. Shi Taifeng (石泰峰), head of the Organization Department since April 2025, was one of Xi’s deputies when Xi was president of the Central Party School, and later served as governor of Jiangsu under Party Secretary—and now second-ranking Politburo Standing Committee member—Li Qiang (李强) ( Xinhua , June 11, 2017; People’s Daily Online , October 25, 2017). In June, the Central Party School presidency went to Cai Qi (蔡奇), Xi’s chief of staff ( Lianhe Zaobao , June 5; Xinhua , June 18). Once a faction’s patron loses favor, its collapse feeds on itself, for three reasons. First, no one will vouch for its members. Under a 2016 Party directive, when officials with a record of poor conduct are promoted (带病提拔), every stage of their selection is reviewed, and the organization departments and leading officials involved are held accountable ( People’s Daily Online , August 29, 2016). To speak up for a member of a fallen faction is to stake one’s own future on him. Second, faction members are now in the way. Every post they hold can go to someone else’s protégés, and those who take over have every incentive to consolidate their positions and none to defend their predecessors. Third, the investigations necessarily target the work that the fallen patron had overseen. In the case of Chen Xi, Cao Xingxin (曹兴信), Chen’s former subordinate at the Organization Department, was investigated in 2024 and punished for having “sought benefits for others in the selection and appointment of officials” (在干部选拔任用工作中为他人谋取利益) (Xinhua, September 28, 2024 , February 24, 2025 ; The Paper , September 28, 2024). As the Organization Department was Chen’s portfolio for a decade, pulling on this thread has led mostly to officials he promoted. And as each cadre has fallen, the remaining members have become more isolated and at the mercy of rivals. Table 1: Fates of Leading Tsinghua Clique Members since the 20th Party Congress Name Post after the 20th Party Congress Outcome Date Chen Xi 陈希 Head of the Organization Department; President of the Central Party School (former Politburo member; vice-national rank) Stepped down from the Organization Department, then the Central Party School April 2023; June 2026 Chen Jining 陈吉宁 Politburo member; Shanghai Party Secretary (vice-national) Under investigation November 2026 Li Ganjie 李干杰 Politburo member; head of the Organization Department from April 2023 (vice-national) Moved to head of the United Front Work Department April 2025 Hu Heping 胡和平 Minister of Culture and Tourism; deputy head of the Propaganda Department (full ministerial) Kept only the Propaganda Department post December 2023 Wang Menghui 王蒙徽 Hubei Party Secretary (full ministerial) Moved near retirement age to vice chair of the NPC Environmental Protection and Resources Conservation Committee December 2024 Liu Ning 刘宁 Guangxi Party Secretary, later Henan Party Secretary (full ministerial) Moved near retirement age to vice chair of the NPC Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee September 2026 Ni Yuefeng 倪岳峰 Hebei Party Secretary (full ministerial) Moved before retirement age to vice chair of the NPC Social Development Affairs Committee July 2026 Wang Xiqin 王希勤 President of Tsinghua University (vice-ministerial) Moved to deputy director of the National Natural Science Foundation; later left the post for undisclosed reasons December 2023; October 2025 Fang Hongwei 方红卫 Shaanxi Party Standing Committee member; Xi’an Party Secretary (vice-ministerial) Under investigation; since indicted November 2025 Qin Weizhong 覃伟中 Shenzhen Mayor (vice-ministerial) Moved to the Party group of the Guangdong Provincial People’s Congress Standing Committee; later placed under investigation September 2026 Xia Linmao 夏林茂 Beijing Party Standing Committee member; vice mayor (vice-ministerial) Under investigation October 2026 Wang Weizhong 王伟中 Guangdong Governor (full ministerial) Promoted to Inner Mongolia Party Secretary September 2025 Yin Yong 殷勇 Beijing Mayor (full ministerial) In office — Chen Xu 陈旭 Deputy head of the United Front Work Department; director of the State Council Overseas Chinese Affairs Office (full ministerial) In office — Liu Xiaokai 刘晓凯 Guizhou CPPCC Chairman (full ministerial) Moved to Yunnan CPPCC Chairman January 2023 Gao Yunlong 高云龙 CPPCC Vice Chairman; Chairman of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce (vice-national) In office — Wang Guangqian 王光谦 Executive Vice Chairman of the China Democratic League; CPPCC Vice Chairman from March 2023 (vice-national) In office — (Source: Author’s compilation from official appointment announcements by Xinhua, People’s Daily Online, the NPC, and others. Besides the 13 officials at full ministerial rank or above, the table lists four vice-ministerial officials: Wang Xiqin, Fang Hongwei, Qin Weizhong, and Xia Linmao.) Chen Jining Had No Record to Shield Himself Chen Jining’s achievements lay in sectoral work. His signature accomplishment came as minister of environmental protection. By 2016, his second year in the post, PM2.5 concentrations in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region had fallen 33 percent from 2013 levels ( People’s Daily Online , January 5, 2017). Yet after becoming Shanghai’s “number one” (一把手), he had little to show for four years at the helm. Instead, the most notable event on his watch was the protest on Urumqi Middle Road less than a month after he took office ( BBC , November 27, 2022; China Brief , December 8, 2022). Though he had little to do with it, it became the first mark on his record. Xi directed Shanghai to make building its “five centers” (五个中心) the main thrust of its work and to “take the lead” (走在前列) in artificial intelligence (AI) (Xinhua, December 3, 2023 , April 29, 2025 ). To this end, Shanghai set up a string of government- and university-branded AI research institutes, established a renminbi (RMB) 22.5 billion ($3.4 billion) AI fund of funds, and in 2025 issued RMB 1 billion ($149 million) in vouchers for computing power, models, and training data in a single round ( SSCI Leading Fund , accessed November 24; Shanghai Municipal Government , July 28, 2025). The spending has not produced convincing results. MiniMax (稀宇科技), Shanghai’s best-known large-model company, fell below its offering price less than a year after listing and is down more than 88 percent from its peak ( Caixin , October 22). Shanghai’s own auditors found that subsidies for three “high-quality incubators” sat idle, that only 33 of the 279 companies backed by an incubator-linked investment fund actually came from incubators, and that RMB 18.5 billion ($2.8 billion) in technology loans had been diverted to urban renewal ( Shanghai Municipal Government , September 20). Shanghai—a higher-ranking municipality directly under the central government—threw the whole city’s resources at AI and still did no better than Hangzhou, which relied on private companies.  [3] This likely disappointed Xi, falling short of both his ambitions and his expectations. Conclusion Chen Jining is the first Politburo member to fall since the Fifth Plenum in late October. The plenum’s Resolution states that the Party has “removed serious dangers hidden within the Party, the state, and the military” (消除了党、国家、军队内部存在的严重隐患), and traces most remaining problems to the officials at all levels who carry out policy ( China Brief , November 18). Less than a month later, accountability for implementation has come down on a Politburo member with an iron fist. Xi had singled out Shanghai to lead in AI. Chen Jining could not deliver, and no one would vouch for him over his other problems. The Resolution also calls for improving “the mechanisms for holding to account those responsible for promoting officials with a record of poor conduct” (干部“带病提拔”责任追究机制) and “firmly eliminating self-serving cliques” (坚决破除“小圈子”) ( Xinhua , November 1). The Tsinghua Clique fits that description—and has consequently lost favor. The rest of Chen Xi’s network can be expected to exit one by one around the 21st Party Congress, and accountability may yet reach Chen Xi himself. Any group that loses Xi’s trust will meet the same fate, as rivals pile on and allies scatter. Notes [1] Here, the Tsinghua Clique refers to officials centered on Chen Xi who studied full-time or worked at Tsinghua, plus his former subordinates at the Organization Department, rather than Tsinghua alumni in general. Xi himself and 20th Politburo members Li Xi (李希) (EMBA), Huang Kunming (黄坤明), and Zhang Guoqing (张国清) (both in-service doctorates) are excluded. On the system for cultivating and transferring cadres that Chen Xi built while running Tsinghua, see Wen-Hsuan Tsai and Xingmiu Liao, “The Impending Rise of the ‘Tsinghua Clique’: Cultivation, Transfer, and Relationships in Chinese Elite Politics,” Journal of Contemporary China 28, no. 120 (2019): 948–64, https://doi.org/10.1080/10670564.2019.1594106 . [2] The 13 are Chen Xi, Chen Jining, Li Ganjie, Hu Heping, Chen Xu, Wang Menghui, Ni Yuefeng, Liu Ning, Wang Weizhong, Yin Yong, Liu Xiaokai, Gao Yunlong, and Wang Guangqian. The count covers the period from the 20th Party Congress to the March 2023 leadership transition and is based on official biographies. In-service graduate degrees and EMBAs are not counted. [3] Hangzhou’s momentum in AI is clearly stronger than Shanghai’s. DeepSeek, Unitree, and the rest of the “six little dragons of Hangzhou” (杭州六小龙) all come from the city ( South China Morning Post , February 10, 2025; China Brief , March 19, 2025). According to a report by the China Academy of Urban Planning and Design, Hangzhou accounted for 16 percent of the notable AI models released worldwide over the past year and a half, the highest share of any Chinese city ( Yicai Global , November 24). The Chinese model most downloaded and most widely adapted in the global open-source community is Alibaba’s Qwen (通义千问), developed in Hangzhou ( Hugging Face , August 14). The post Fall of Politburo’s Chen Jining Marks End of Tsinghua Clique appeared first on Jamestown .

title: Hong Kong’s Police Training Advances Beijing’s Global Reach
zh_title: 香港警察培训提升北京的全球影响力
summary: 内容提要 香港新成立的警察学院为北京提供了一种通过国际公认的机构输出中国安全实践的途径。随着北京的警察机构与中华人民共和国的警察机构趋同，这座城市剩余的独特性可能对北京变得更有用。英国的学术声望可以促进香港警务转型。受过剑桥大学培训的导师可以为当地学位提供可信度，重现中国机构的优先事项，从而使代际变革能够在不立即与剑桥大学决裂的情况下继续进行。
content:
内容提要 香港新成立的警察学院为北京提供了一种通过国际公认的机构输出中国安全实践的途径。随着北京的警察机构与中华人民共和国的警察机构趋同，这座城市剩余的独特性可能对北京变得更有用。英国的学术声望可以促进香港警务转型。剑桥大学培训的导师可以为复制中国机构优先事项的本地学位提供可信度，从而允许代际变革在不立即打​​破英国教育传统的情况下进行。海外培训可以塑造对中国装备的需求，并培养外国安全机构内部的联系。将指导与采购和专业标准联系起来还可以将北京的影响力从个别官员扩展到受援机构的运作方式。 11月11日，香港国际警务学院揭牌，并与柬埔寨和沙特阿拉伯的警察学院签署培训协议（香港警务处，11月11日）。除了这个国际平台之外，学院还将提供专门从事安全和刑事调查的应用学位课程（香港电台 [RTHK]，10 月 9 日）。这些举措将在国内培养政治上可靠的官员与输出香港的专业声誉联系起来。
北京将获得一个培训体系，其国际身份仍明显保留香港的特色，但其机构内容越来越多地反映中国公共安全的优先事项。 学院扩展香港的警察外交 学院的目标是通过 20 多个项目和论坛，每年培训约 1,000 名警官，其中包括约 200 名海外人员（香港政府，11 月 11 日）。课程涵盖刑事调查和反恐、战术指挥和情报等更敏感的职能。只有五名官员将协调现有的培训资源（文汇报，10 月 9 日）。因此，香港可以通过汇集其警察机构内现有的专业知识来扩大其外交作用。香港警方最近与柬埔寨警察学院、澳大利亚警察管理学院、埃及警察学院和哈萨克斯坦阿拉木图学院合作（另类，2025年12月17日；香港警务处，11月13日访问）。这些关系的范围从交流到培训外国教练。香港于2026年3月培训柬埔寨战术教官，并与荷兰、泰国、新加坡和越南进行交流（另类，2025年6月11日；4月15日；大公报，5月23日）。将这些联系纳入一个共同机构可以使香港成为海外官员专业发展的经常参考点。
领导人论坛将针对东南亚、中东和其他“一带一路”合作伙伴（香港警务处，11月11日）。香港即将主办国际刑事警察组织（国际刑警组织）大会，香港海关担任世界海关组织亚太区副主席，为推动“一国两制”提供平台（文汇报，10月9日；香港海关，10月） 15）。这一框架利用香港的国际地位来支持这样的说法，即香港保留着独特的、与全球相连的地位。

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary Hong Kong’s new police academy offers Beijing a way to export Chinese security practices through an internationally recognizable institution. The city’s remaining distinctiveness may become more useful to Beijing as its police institutions converge with those of the People’s Republic of China’s (PRC). British academic prestige can facilitate Hong Kong’s policing transition. Cambridge University-trained supervisors can lend credibility to a local degree that reproduces Chinese institutional priorities, allowing generational change to proceed without an immediate break with British educational traditions. Overseas training can shape demand for Chinese equipment and cultivate contacts inside foreign security institutions. Linking instruction to procurement and professional standards also could extend Beijing’s influence beyond individual officers into how recipient agencies operate. On November 11, Hong Kong inaugurated its International Academy of Policing and signed training agreements with police academies in Cambodia and Saudi Arabia ( Hong Kong Police Force , November 11). Alongside this international platform, the academy will offer an applied degree program specializing in security and criminal investigations ( Radio Television Hong Kong [RTHK] , October 9). These initiatives link the cultivation of politically reliable officers at home with the export of Hong Kong’s professional reputation. Beijing stands to gain a training system whose international identity remains recognizably Hong Kong’s but whose institutional content increasingly reflects Chinese public security priorities. The Academy Extends Hong Kong’s Police Diplomacy The academy aims to train approximately 1,000 officers annually, including around 200 overseas personnel, through more than 20 programs and forums ( Hong Kong Government , November 11). Courses span criminal investigation and more sensitive functions such as counterterrorism, tactical command, and intelligence. Just five officers will coordinate existing training resources ( Wen Wei Po , October 9). Hong Kong can therefore expand its diplomatic role by pooling expertise already available within its police institutions. Hong Kong’s police have recently worked with Cambodia’s Police Academy, the Australian Institute of Police Management, Egypt’s Police Academy, and Kazakhstan’s Almaty Academy ( Offbeat , December 17, 2025; Hong Kong Police Force , accessed November 13). These relationships range from exchanges to training foreign instructors. Hong Kong trained Cambodian tactical instructors in March 2026, and held exchanges with the Netherlands, Thailand, Singapore, and Vietnam (Offbeat, June 11, 2025 ; April 15 ; Ta Kung Pao , May 23). Bringing these contacts into a common institution can make Hong Kong a recurring reference point in overseas officers’ professional development. Leadership forums will target Southeast Asian, Middle Eastern, and other One Belt One Road (OBOR) partners ( Hong Kong Police Force , November 11). Hong Kong’s forthcoming hosting of the International Criminal Police Organization (INTERPOL) General Assembly and its Customs service’s Asia-Pacific vice-chairmanship of the World Customs Organization offer platforms for promoting “one country, two systems” (一國兩制) ( Wen Wei Po , October 9; Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department , October 15). This framing uses Hong Kong’s international standing to support the claim that the city retains a distinct and globally connected role under Chinese sovereignty. Participation in the Association of Police Training Institutions in Asia and Dubai’s international policing best-practice conference provides established channels (Offbeat, April 22, 2015 , December 23, 2020 ). These forums could give Hong Kong a wider role in defining the terms of international police cooperation. Training Can Export an Integrated Policing System Hong Kong offers Beijing an intermediary whose international credibility partly rests on relationships predating its convergence with the People’s Republic of China’s (PRC) public security system. Foreign agencies may find cooperation with Hong Kong easier to justify than direct engagement with Chinese public security authorities. Expertise acquired through international partnerships can be adapted to Chinese priorities and circulated under a familiar institutional identity. Hong Kong’s distinctiveness can thus lower the political barriers to accepting Chinese policing practices. This advantage depends on partners continuing to treat Hong Kong’s police as institutionally distinct. The potential export is an integrated system of operations, equipment, organization, and training. Teaching officers how to identify threats and organize a response also shapes which capabilities they consider necessary. If these methods become routine, Chinese influence can persist beyond the course itself, embedded in everyday institutional decisions. A regular role in multilateral training, potentially through INTERPOL-related cooperation, could also confer authority over professional standards. Selecting which threats deserve attention and which responses count as best practice can give Chinese security assumptions the status of technical expertise. Recipient agencies could absorb those assumptions through professional learning without making an explicit political commitment to Beijing. Training also offers access to foreign officers’ institutional priorities, procedures, and vulnerabilities, creating opportunities for intelligence collection and cultivation. Alumni networks could serve united-front objectives by sustaining contacts inside overseas security establishments. These remain potential uses of the relationships, not demonstrated activities of the academy. Where security-sector reform connects policing with border management, intelligence, disaster response, or military organizations, shared personnel and practices could carry that influence into the wider security apparatus. Police Education Cultivates Political Reliability At home, the degree conferred by the training program opens a door for integration within Hong Kong’s political elite. Full police funding gives serving officers without a first degree an incentive to participate ( RTHK , October 9). This builds on a model pioneered by Tsinghua University, which launched its Executive Master of Public Administration program for Hong Kong governance professionals in 2018. Alumni reported in May 2025 included constitutional affairs official Clement Woo (胡健民), the chief executive’s special assistant Jenny Wong (黃芷淵), and legislators Carmen Kan (簡慧敏), Shang Hailong (尚海龍), Edward Leung (梁熙), and Gary Zhang (張欣宇) ( Ta Kung Pao , May 17, 2025). It also builds on a separate Police College partnership, formalized in 2021, which was renewed in 2023 for three further cohorts ( Offbeat , May 24, 2023). The new degree program emerges during a period in which Hong Kong’s police force is already undergoing practical and symbolic convergence with the PRC. Chinese-style foot drills became standard in 2022 ( Deutsche Welle , January 14, 2022). Earlier revisions to its published history removed or softened references to the 1989 pro-democracy movement and the 1967 riots ( Radio France Internationale , July 19, 2016). A phased replacement program introduced Chinese-made CF98-A and CS/LP5 pistols from 2024. By May 2026, police had also confirmed adoption of CS/LS7 submachine guns by the Counter Terrorism Response Unit and Airport Security Unit ( Xinhua , November 18, 2024; China News Service , May 7). Academic credentials follow these means of institutionalizing the transition. Political education and technological familiarization already form part of professional training. The People’s Public Security University of China has hosted Hong Kong police study programs since 2001 ( People’s Public Security University of China , May 18, 2011). Partnerships also include Shanghai Police College and Guangdong Police College. A January 2024 agreement with the PRC Ministry of Public Security expanded the “6+2” training framework to “6+2+N,” which included six study programs at police institutions, two exchange programs for police tactical instructors, and multiple programs on the PRC’s national affairs. A 2023 university study program combined police developments with teaching on the Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) 20th National Congress and a visit to Huawei’s Beijing research institute (Offbeat, August 16, 2023 ; January 8, 2025 ). A Hong Kong police alumni association for the People’s Public Security University of China was established in 2006, and the university’s then-president, Wang Yanji (王彦吉), attended its inauguration ( Offbeat , November 22, 2006). In November 2024, two superintendents and three Police College staff joined national affairs training organized by Renmin University and Beijing’s Liaison Office in Hong Kong ( Offbeat , January 22, 2025). The inclusion of teaching staff extends the reach of exchanges, because their experience can shape the curriculum for subsequent cohorts. Hong Kong’s very firstfive-year plan (2026–2030), unveiled in September 2026, explicitly connects regular training cooperation with institutions in the PRC to strengthening civil servants’ patriotic commitment ( Hong Kong Government , September 16). The new degree can give that objective a continuing institutional form. British Credentials Can Ease Institutional Change What sets Hong Kong’s police degree apart from other programs is its supervisory arrangement. Final projects are to be supervised by officers of superintendent rank or above with qualifications from Tsinghua or Cambridge University in the United Kingdom, building authority through academic pedigree ( RTHK , October 9). Hong Kong’s collaboration with Cambridge on the Master of Studies in Applied Criminology and Police Management began in 2017. Senior officers completed the course, and Cambridge academics traveled to Hong Kong for dissertation presentations and alumni exchanges ( Offbeat , December 18, 2019). These relationships supplied expertise and an internationally recognizable mark of professional status that remains available to officers trained under the earlier arrangement. Cambridge still advertises its police executive master’s program, despite the United Kingdom suspending military training for Hong Kong police in 2020 ( The Observer , August 15, 2020; University of Cambridge , accessed November 13). Hong Kong police sponsorship arrangements remain unclear, as a supervisor’s Cambridge qualification does not imply Cambridge oversight of the new degree. This gives British academic prestige a new political use: British-trained officers can validate a locally controlled degree whose graduates enter an institution increasingly shaped by Chinese priorities. As British institutional influence gradually recedes, Hong Kong is trying to establish its own prestigious academic institutions. Creating local degrees that offer sufficient recognition and career opportunities would weaken demand for overseas study, reducing the political cost of changing the force’s educational orientation. Under “patriots administering Hong Kong” (愛國者治港), familiarity with the PRC’s governance and Hong Kong’s circumstances (知國情、懂港情) may increasingly function as an informal credential for political office ( Wen Wei Po , January 24, 2021). The degree could give that political expectation a routine place in police career development. Training Connects Officers to Chinese Suppliers The 2026 Global Public Security Cooperation Forum in Lianyungang combined an equipment exhibition with initiatives on public security standardization and international police education ( Xinhua , September 9). Local authorities promoted exports of Chinese security technologies, equipment, and integrated systems through the city’s security-industry platform ( Lianyungang Fabu , September 9). Bringing training and suppliers into the same cooperation agenda can help Chinese products become familiar answers to the operational problems foreign officers are taught to address. Hong Kong’s police academy already provides a concrete connection. On November 4, Offbeat , the force’s official journal, reported that its Advanced Tactics Application Course would include visits to firearms and ammunition factories in the PRC ( Offbeat , November 4). Such visits make suppliers part of professional instruction. If agencies adopt the associated equipment and routines, maintenance, software, and retraining costs can make switching systems harder, locking the force in to dependence on PRC supply chains. Where suppliers and technologies serve both policing and defense, these relationships could also support military–civil fusion. Communications, surveillance, and border management provide plausible points of overlap. Procurement choices originating in police training could spread through shared personnel, equipment, and operating practices, connecting a wider range of security institutions to Chinese supply chains. Conclusion Under Hong Kong’s diminishing autonomy, its police force seeks to retain a British-derived professional identity while Chinese institutions increasingly shape how officers are trained and equipped. This combination uses credibility accumulated under an earlier political order to advance Chinese security priorities. Abroad, it offers a way to embed Chinese practices in institutions that might resist an overt partnership with PRC institutions. Its new International Academy of Policing could turn the distinction promised by “one country, two systems” into a means of extending one system’s influence overseas. The post Hong Kong’s Police Training Advances Beijing’s Global Reach appeared first on Jamestown .

title: 宏福苑居民的災後一年，走不出的精神困獸鬥

content: 11月中一個下午，歐太約定街坊回到宏福苑附近走走。 「我們要挑戰龍潭虎穴。」她說。 造成168人死、79傷的宏福苑大火已經過去一年。如今八幢大樓靜默，而在下方的綠植公園，倖存的宏福苑居民接連接受香港和外媒記者訪問，講述著劫後生活。這裡曾經是大火後的民間獻花公園，如今政府拉起了一條黃黑線，劃出區域。 在這傷感的時刻，四散的街坊在宏福苑打照面。除了互相擁抱問候，他們還有一個類似的遭遇——每當有居民接受訪問，附近警察會來了解一下，看看媒體的證件。當居民與記者在宏福苑外圍拍攝，也被當值警察問及詳情。 「11月開始明顯敏感了。之前影相不理會的，但近期會觸動他們的神經。」宏泰閣居民及大火遺屬葉家駒對端傳媒形容：「宏福苑差不多成為不可提的三個字。」 2026年11月15日，大埔聖母無玷之心堂舉行宏福苑週年追思彌撒。攝：鄧家烜/端傳媒 11月15日，大埔聖母無玷之心堂舉行宏福苑週年追思彌撒，指曾有警察查詢活動，堂區一度在活動主題中抽走「宏福苑」字眼。也有居民向端傳媒透露，一些關注居民情緒的活動在租場時遇上困難，最終活動主題沒有宏福苑三個字。一個原訂在週年前夕公演和發布、由受災外傭和救援者撰寫的劇場和新書，主辦指有不可預期因素取消演出。 傳媒報導也受限。宏泰閣居民歐太說，有電視台拍攝她和其他居民的週年報導，經多番修改後，最終仍被抽起，未有播出。宏盛閣居民何佩珊（Betty）記得，上樓執拾當天，曾有記者向她說，公司不想他們訪問居民，只需訪問司長巡視現場。 11月26日這天，要怎樣悼念，居民開始變得謹慎。 葉家駒很確定，一定會回去悼念太太白瑞蓮。但是，「如果我在那裡出現的話，會引起麻煩，我不想被人感覺藉著這件事去挑動所謂矛盾。」受訪者不約而同提到，不會約街坊前往宏福苑悼念，只會自己去，以免招人話柄；也不會在通訊群組中分享自己會不會去悼念、幾點去悼念。 這年間，Betty 覺得除了受訪，很難表達自己的意願。她曾打算在自己物業的窗外掛上「原址重建」的標語，但未掛起已被警方勸止。「既然大樓已經堅決要拆，為什麼不讓街坊完成自己的心願？」 她善於隱藏情緒，大火後甚少流淚，但那次她走到地面便哭了出來——她覺得自己被消音了。她擔心宏福苑事件正在淡化，或許很快，再沒有人記得他們這一年經歷了什麼。 持續追蹤後續報道 免費註冊端傳媒，不錯過最新消息，與我們保持連結 立即註冊 .nc-loop-dots-4-24-icon-o{--animation-duration:0.8s} .nc-loop-dots-4-24-icon-o *{opacity:.4;transform:scale(.75);animation:nc-loop-dots-4-anim var(--animation-duration) infinite} .nc-loop-dots-4-24-icon-o :nth-child(1){transform-origin:4px 12px;animation-delay:-.3s;animation-delay:calc(var(--animation-duration)/-2.666)} .nc-loop-dots-4-24-icon-o :nth-child(2){transform-origin:12px 12px;animation-delay:-.15s;animation-delay:calc(var(--animation-duration)/-5.333)} .nc-loop-dots-4-24-icon-o :nth-child(3){transform-origin:20px 12px} @keyframes nc-loop-dots-4-anim{0%,100%{opacity:.4;transform:scale(.75)}50%{opacity:1;transform:scale(1)}} Email sent! Check your inbox to complete your signup. 註冊後可自由選擇接收的電子報，並可隨時取消訂閱或停止接收通知。 精神的困獸鬥 2025年11月26日下午2點33分，大埔宏福苑起火，連燒43小時始救熄。 大火後初期，70歲的宏仁閣居民許太感覺到丈夫有點異常。他不再開口說話，連最親的人也不願意聯絡。「一合上眼就看見火。」他說。 精神科醫生說丈夫因為目擊火災，恐慌狀況嚴重，給他們開了藥。那段時間，他們在過渡性房屋的爭吵增加。許太的枕頭上，常常有一堆無故掉落的頭髮。其實她也受影響，看著坊間有聲音說他們已被賠了許多錢，令她覺得只有居民能講心底話，拒接其他人打來的電話。 新年後，丈夫慢慢適應生活。得知2028年會搬入新屋後，他們決定在臨時居所安置在災場取回的先母神主牌，丈夫才終於放鬆下來，「知道自己有能做的事，就好多了。」 許太自覺比丈夫更平靜，方法是大火之後，「從不主動再看新聞。」 2025年12月6日，宏福苑火災現場下的獻花區。攝：林振東/端傳媒 大火即將一年之際，精神健康諮詢委員會主席林正財 透露 ，有200位宏福苑居民需轉介至心理學家、臨床心理學家及精神科醫生接受高密度心理治療。協助失去親人的「守望．同行」計劃至今接觸156個家庭；3300名居民透過「凝聚．同行」計劃獲得大學、非政府機構及專業團體的支援和評估，約1800人接受了小組、個人輔導等低密度支援。 國際創傷照護專家 Jennifer Wild 曾參與倫敦 Grenfell Tower 大火的心理支援工作，大火後兩個月，她受邀到香港與林正財對談災難創傷。她在講座上提到：「火災是最嚴重的創傷之一，因為人們因此失去家園。」她治療過的火災倖存者，比其他類型的創傷更為複雜；她特別提到大埔火災不少倖存者是長者、外傭和小孩，是相對弱勢的群體。 當時她指出，社群要走復元之路有幾個重點，其中包括與受災者見面，「真正傾聽社區的聲音，並與社區一起共同制定優先事項。」第二點則是確保透明度與問責。她說，倫敦當時有1億英鎊投入復原計劃，「Grenfell 倖存者和相關團體想知道人們繳的稅金是如何分配的，他們對此非常積極發聲。這正是透明度與問責的重要之處。」 她亦認為要先確保倖存者有安全居所，才能著手處理他們的心理健康。 45歲的歐太數算著，相熟的宏福朋友中，八九成在看心理學家，三分一左右在看精神科；然而後者可能顧忌社會目光，是相對隱形的。 2026年10月29日，宏福苑居民歐太觀看大埔宏福苑火災獨立委員會的報告記者會電視直播，行政長官李家超率領相關官員道歉。攝：鄧家烜/端傳媒 初期安頓家人後，歐太安排了3個兒子接受輔導，當時輔導員認為全家人也有輔導需要。歐太於是也開始見心理學家，她想只要跟對方聊聊天，便能釋放壓力。但當決定不向政府賣出業權，她雖覺得捱過一關，情緒卻沒有好轉，「最初以為賣樓死線後就完，但不是，那只是一個新開始——如何重新建立一個家，全都是一關接一關。」 她本對精神科有些抗拒，想給自己多點時間。但當聽到新聞提到不賣樓，物業價值或會歸零時，她開始無法進食、常常頭暈，體重掉了21公斤。晚上她也無法入睡，常常張開眼等天光。八九月，她在醫院驗出貧血，醫生問她生活有什麼變化，她回答說自己是宏福苑災民。醫生立即將她轉介精神科，幾天後便能看診，她也嚇著了。「香港醫療體制，一般要等很久的吧。」 在精神科門口面前，她坐了一會，才走進去。 她確診創傷後遺症和抑鬱症，最近開始服抗抑鬱藥、鎮靜和助眠藥物；還未計其他胃藥和維他命。這一年，她因為聽過火災現場的聲音，常覺得周圍很嘈吵；她亦覺得特別冷，夏天也用披肩包住自己。這是身體的高警覺狀態，「身體告訴你還在火災中，所以你不需睡覺，不需進食。」 有一次，她參與大火前就開始的社區活動。活動影片記錄了參與者這一年的臉容，她看見自己以前由心而發的笑容，到最近的笑容，「我知道是一個面具，想人見到我的堅強。」這觸發她劇烈的心跳和手震：「原來我看起來像一個人，但一年後，不再是個完整的人。」 這是一場精神的困獸鬥。她想，她終於要承認軟弱，並承認一年後，她無法接受這場大火。她覺得，能夠公開說出自己作為宏福苑居民在看精神科，或許能令其他居民覺得被理解，可以接受自己。 「無論關於宏福苑的事，抑或是我們看醫生的事，被理解是很重要。」她說。「政府用行政作考慮，有些政策我理解的，如果你不強硬，你很難做到。但是居民的精神健康是不是真的可以承受到這種壓力呢？」 宏盛閣居民何佩珊（Betty）著重人生規劃，花了18年時間完成宏盛閣的按揭貸款，為自己準備退休的安身之所，她不想輕言放棄。攝：林振東/端傳媒 賣業權：選擇的權利 大火後一年，居民的壓力層層疊加。 今年5月底，Betty 第一次拆開政府的收購業權意向書，只是為了拍照給記者。8月31日是政府收購宏福苑業權的最後期限，她最終還是拒絕出售宏盛閣的家。 「年初政府開始做問卷的時候，我已經決定不會賣。」她說。今年1月，政府向居民發問卷，收集他們對長遠安置的初步意願，提到原址重建料需時約10年，Betty 填選了原址重建的選項。61歲的她著重人生規劃，花了18年時間完成宏盛閣的按揭貸款，為自己準備退休的安身之所，她不想輕言放棄。 這份初步意向調查顯示， 逾7成宏福苑業主考慮出售業權 ，有22%業主期望政府提供包含「原址重建」的安置方案。最終，初步意向書變成政府2月提出的長遠安置方案：以未補價8000港元呎價、已補地價10500港元呎價收購單位，政府指高於市價約三分之一。 港府表明傾向拆除宏福苑，不會原址重建或修復；同時間，立法會議員何君堯、管浩鳴首次公開稱不接受收購方案的業主為「釘子戶」。 作為問卷裡僅接受原址重建的9%，Betty 最無法接受的，是房屋局至今未公開宏福苑的驗樓報告，業主無法按實際情況判斷。包括她在內的 居民 和媒體多番按《公開資料守則》向房屋局 索取驗樓報告 ，被局方以將有雨季風季、樓宇結構安全需持續監測、披露未完成分析資料或令人誤解為由，拒絕公開。 Betty多次出席宏福苑大火聽證會。攝：林振東/端傳媒 6月，Betty 離開大火聽證會時，接到房屋局負責跟進賣樓的解說員電話。對方遊說她填妥出售意向書，Betty 每當聽到解說員口中的金額，只覺得非常煩躁。她態度堅決，決定不進入爭先後的賣樓戰場——遞交出售業權意向的日期先後，會影響選購新樓的先後次序，第一輪定在6月30日，第二輪定在8月31日。 第一輪死線，逾85.6%宏福苑業主接受收購。時任房屋局長何永賢公布數字時，曾以「節節高升」形容升幅，引發居民不滿，斥其「白事當紅事辦」。 行會成員陳克勤曾指，不賣樓的話物業價值有機會歸零，對香港勞苦大眾來說，三四百萬港元歸零並不是小事。「現在不單是我條氣不順，很多街坊條氣也不順。你估街坊真的想賣樓嗎？」曾有街坊向她表達恐懼，問她應否賣樓，也有人向她道歉，說無法陪她堅持到最後。有些業主則選擇消極表達訴求，直至最後才遞交意向書及最後一批揀樓，也不後悔。 「大家街坊都知道，你有一家大細還怎樣堅持？」她安慰對方。她想像要是媽媽仍與她同住，她也會忍痛賣樓。但現在的她，除了仍在安老院的媽媽外，孑然一身。 最後，拒絕出售業權的業主由8月底的45戶，逐步降至最後的13戶。而政府一方表示，明年立法收回業權可能性極高。 政府收購業權時，一併取得本屬於業主的20億港元的火險索償權，Betty 對此感到困惑。而400萬港元或會歸零，她的態度始終如一。「賭一舖囉，總之你拿得到便拿去吧。全世界看著你，如果是真的歸零，我不相信這件事沒有人報導。」 她嘆一口氣說，「距離失去宏福苑越來越近，可以用一個『慘』字形容。」 以為還在宏福苑 大埔生活的記憶和景象，是僅存的憑據。 大火初期，歐太見政府和非牟利機構迅速投入協助，尤其是一戶一社工的安排令她安心。直到政府以私人公司收購宏福苑的信寄來，「那一刻真的直插谷底……為什麼所有選項，第一個都是賣宏福苑？」 宏泰閣居民歐太和先生商量後決定不出售宏福苑的業權。攝：鄧家烜/端傳媒 七八月，歐太和先生也決定不出售業權。他們的考慮有幾項：收購方案不足以在大埔區購入類近宏福苑呎數的單位，供一家六人入住；居民在死線前未等到調查報告，政府也從沒公布過驗樓報告。政府解說員來電時曾勸她住遠一點、住小一點，她說自己雖然不幸，但起碼有基本權利選擇。「如果以後小朋友來問我，為什麼還有很多的不明不白，像驗樓報告、獨立調查報告，為什麼你不等，你就去賣業權呢？」 「我們應該有選擇的權利。」她說。 「尊重私有物業產權的話，聆聽民意的話，有人願意賣，那你同樣要接納和包容有人不想賣。」歐太感覺到，面前的路越來越窄，窄到只夠她一個人、或者幾個人通過。「如果我看到前景，有信心可以安居樂業，那我就賣給你了。我由頭到尾都不是要令政府難做的。」 她說，「因為99.1％（賣業權），只剩下13戶（不賣），沒有事情可以發生的了。」 不甘與猜忌 不過，對大多數居民來說，賣業權是唯一選擇。 宏志閣業主 Mike 早年購入宏福苑獨居。宏志閣因為未有被燒毀，居民們曾經覺得有一線機會能回家居住。及至3月，工聯會立法會議員鄧家彪指，接獲逾半宏志閣業主聯繫，希望政府能一併收購宏志閣。其後有出席聽證會的宏志閣業主 質疑 ，有人慫恿居民聯絡工聯會賣樓。3個月後，政府稱接獲四分三宏志閣業主希望被收購業權，把宏志閣納入收購計劃。 過去一年，他認為政府處理災民的政策多變，例如初步意向書取得的數據，事後成為最終否決原址重建的理據。「你的每一個變化，我們也要用很多精神和能力去適應。」這年間，Mike  對於轉變已逐漸麻木，「能有什麼感覺？我們有好多不忿、心裏話，我們當然想拿回公道，但是連說話的機會也沒有。」 宏志閣業主 Mike 觀察到街坊敢怒不敢言，一些人變得害怕接受訪問。攝：林振東/端傳媒 Mike 說，業主最初曾想一起討論業權問題，但每一步也感到被阻撓。宏福苑業主三四月曾兩度爭取召開業主大會，但有份發起連署、經常接受訪問的業主江祥發於5月突然被警方拘捕。案情指江及其太太涉詐騙及洗黑錢，具體內容與宏福苑無關，而他獲釋後未再就宏福苑發表任何言論。事後，Mike 觀察到街坊敢怒不敢言，一些人變得害怕接受訪問。 「我們只是想開業主大會，為何有那麼多阻撓？」即使7月中成功召開業主大會，業主聯署爭取的議程卻一一被刪減，包括要求政府公開樓宇勘查報告、允許業主多次返回單位收拾等等。 一連串操作下，Mike 覺得自己不像災民，更像是因發展收地而被逼遷的村民。 面對長遠安置方案，除非居民選擇領取現金，否則無可避免要與鄰里爭先作出決定。政府災後提出的特設銷售計劃，業主可選取房委會及房協下的資助項目，單位遍及啟德、粉嶺、將軍澳等地。若想選購位處市區的兩房單位而售價較收購價貴，他們便要重新貸款供樓。此外，居民亦要先抽籤取得揀樓的先後次序，籌號較前的購入心儀單位的機會較大，靠後的居民機會變小。 「為什麼變成把我們丟到一個鬥獸環境裡，互相廝殺去爭兩房單位？而且我們還要重新供樓？」他說，不少居民覺得，自己是「踩住其他人才能買樓」。 從一開始政府宣布收購，到立法會議員形容不願賣樓的居民為「釘子戶」，34歲的 Dorz 一早有心理準備，情況會往最壞的地步走。 Dorz 是第一批選擇賣樓的住戶，並在8月中正式賣樓。和88歲的嫲嫲、妹妹生活的他，最大的考慮是希望嫲嫲盡快定下來。「如果不是老人家，我真的企硬爭取到最後，但是沒辦法。」他唯有拖延一會才交表，在數據上盡量支持不願賣樓的街坊。 他們揀樓抽籤排得較前，居民恭喜他，但他並不開心，「你會想其他人怎麼辦？這件事不值得慶賀，大家同一個屋苑，面對同一件事。」他曾遇上一個街坊對他不斷懺悔，「她說不想賣，也哭了，覺得好像對不起他們（不賣樓的居民）。上了年紀的很無奈，即將或已退休的也有，難道瞓街嗎？」 他說，不排除有居民很隨遇而安，但他在群組看見的居民，「大家都是不開心的。」 Dorz 是第一批選擇賣樓的住戶，和88歲的嫲嫲、妹妹生活的他，最大的考慮是希望嫲嫲盡快定下來。攝：林振東/端傳媒 「大家都會很害怕，如果我錯過了，是不是就落後於人？」近半年，歐太也觀察到居民在通訊群組討論賣樓，時會引發爭執。例如當討論是否要簽意向書時，有居民叫大家不要簽，但有居民會擔心：這樣提議的人，是不是想鬥快抽樓？ 這跟上樓安排類似——自四五月以來，政府准許居民回家執拾，但後續安排蘊釀了猜忌和不快。早前，政府承諾只要向社工申請就能再上樓，及後未再公布日子。8月底，卻有消息指少數居民「被選中」上樓，政府始確認曾安排超過10戶上樓執拾。截至11月，政府指已安排80個住戶上樓，但未回應是否要經警方批准、獲批理由為何等等。 居民驚訝之餘，也紛紛猜測上樓的條件，打聽獲選者的狀況：是不是要簽意向書賣樓？抑或已經正式買了新屋？最初若獲安排上樓，居民都會本著互助心態分享，但當其他人不斷追問，便會造成壓力。歐太提到，後來一些人上樓後才分享狀況，她估計是怕上樓機會被影響。 她對此感覺很差。她覺得，大火後居民之間互相支持才能一同捱過日子，但無論是出售業權的死線，抑或是上樓的猜測，都讓業主群產生了裂痕。為了不傷感情，大家逐漸從大群組轉到小群組，或只是和相熟街坊分享想法。「慢慢，大家身邊的支援網絡越來越小。」 「大家已經這麼難捱，你還要因為不公開、不透明，令大家猜忌。其實我們都是返自己單位而已，為什麼要搞到影響街坊互相的信任度？」她說，居民面對的是人生重大決定，如果政策公開透明，「大家會過得舒服點，起碼大家知道是公平的。由開始揀樓、賣樓到現在，街坊經常會講『公不公平』，大家很想知道準則在哪裏，但不知道準則的時候，就只有猜忌。當大家的關係有猜忌，就很難再去面對每一天。」 透過社工、解說員、媒體，「我們一直都有發聲，但是大家的聲音好像越來越小，政府越來越聽不見我們的聲音，大家、居民和政府的距離越來越遠。」她說，如果能聆聽他們的需要，政策落實就能更精準。「其實很簡單，我們都只不過是想被聆聽。」 宏泰閣居民葉家駒的太太白瑞蓮在火中罹難。攝：馮凱鍵/端傳媒 遺屬：問責是否足夠？ 前運輸及房屋局局長張炳良11月初於《明報》 撰文 ，以「宏福苑慘劇之痛 能否『解結』？」為題，指解結重點有三：一、處理災戶安居及業權安排；二、釐清真相，追究責任；三、徹底檢討，整頓改革。 對於業權，他提到房屋局確定房屋未能修茸，亦早已否定原址重建，但至今仍未公開屋宇檢測報告；現時有未願出售業權的業主，在《基本法》保障私人產權下，立法強購須慎重處理。他建議應盡早公布驗樓報告釋疑。 「過去一年政府欲做『好事』，部分業主卻認為另有企圖……善後卻衍生互信危機，反映解說及解讀均出了問題。」他寫道。 68歲的宏泰閣居民及遺屬葉家駒向端傳媒表示，居民最關心的問題有二，「一個是問責問題，另一個是大家都很憤怒的安置問題。」他主要關注問責部分。 自從太太白瑞蓮在火中罹難，這一年來，在大火聽證會、承建商被控誤殺的庭審，葉家駒從未缺席。聽證會最初，他覺得獨立委員會主席陸啟康的開場振振有詞，對調查有所期望。但後來聽證會未升格，無法傳召承建商、顧問公司代表等人出庭，而政府代表律師又指出政府被不法商人瞞騙，他逐漸覺得聽證會能追責的範圍有限。而委員會代表資深大律師杜淦堃的陳詞，痛陳建築公司、政府部門和私營機構，對他而言，已是最後的公道說話。 所以，港府公開調查報告前的那個早上，他傳訊息給太太的 WhatsApp 號碼：「我也沒什麼期望。」 宏泰閣居民葉家駒不斷提起近月來香港爆出的工程醜聞，覺得醜聞反映宏福苑大火揭發的只是冰山一角，亦非個別事件。攝：林振東/端傳媒 獨立委員會報告最終揭示火災由一個煙頭引起，加上承建商使用助燃維修物料、火警鐘等防護系統失效，並點名4個政府監管部門失職。報告並羅列 120項 建議，包括即時禁止使用危險物料，長遠堵塞監管漏洞，打擊圍標等 。 港府稱 ，至11月下旬，已落實29項建議；跨部門打擊樓宇維修工程圍標聯合特遣隊，成立約一個月採取兩次行動，總共拘捕163人。 大火後337天，特首李家超終率領高官首次就大火致歉。當下葉家駒更在乎道歉的內容：「不是在乎他十秒二十秒，甚至鞠躬一分鐘，而是要用行動讓人看到你覺得愧疚，然後道歉。」 他認為，目前的問責程度只是精準的「納米級」，只有被點名失職決策局的房屋局長何永賢請辭、而非下台；對於保安局、發展局、勞福局等的追責亦未足夠。「大火到現在，政府給我們見到的，很全力開行馬力去做的，只是收購業權。」他說面對錯失的過程，「是痛的，不是很多人能夠忍受到的，但如果你連這個勇氣都沒有，其他都不用說。」 張炳良的評論也觸及問責。他提到問責考驗行政長官的政治倫理觀念、判斷民情與政治的智慧，也看委任主要官員的中央政府如何取捨定斷。「一國兩制下，非單由涉事官員或行政長官決定『去留』。」對於有聲音質疑為何只有一個官員問責下台，「雖行政長官說乃其『政治決定』不一定足以釋疑，」他寫道：「惟有時現實就是如此。」 問責以外，葉家駒認為改革未夠全面。他指改革主力針對圍標，但宏福苑災難不只是承建商問題，還牽涉到政府監管、負責人的處事態度，「這是根深蒂固需要連根拔起的問題。」 「圍標多年，為何要等到宏福苑大火後，才短時間瓦解這麼大的圍標集團？以前是不知道，抑或不去做？」他說這是災民心裡的問號。他又認為，報告仍然缺失了幾塊拼圖：前大埔區議員黃碧嬌、物業管理公司置邦的物管經理、前法團主席鄧國權等等。 在訪問的路上，葉家駒不斷提起近月香港爆出的工程醜聞。看到諸如赤柱豪宅 ONE STANLEY 被揭發缺鋼筋、瑪麗醫院升降機事故及井道傾斜等等新聞，他的心情很複雜。他覺得，醜聞反映宏福苑大火揭發的只是冰山一角，亦非個別事件，「工程界已經爛透了。感受最深的是，宏福苑出了那麼大件事，都沒有汲取教訓……」 「如果連168人的犧牲都喚不醒政府的警覺，他們是死得更無辜。」他最大的擔憂是，當城市沒有汲取教訓，「災難只有越來越多，甚至越來越嚴重。」 他希望爭取就宏福苑大火召開死因研訊。此外，部分人正循法律援助計劃，追討傷亡賠償。 宏福苑居民謝先生，背後是早前活動上市民為宏福苑居民打氣的心意卡。攝：林振東/端傳媒 同行渡劫難 每次在宏福苑接受訪問，47歲的居民謝先生總是言辭辛辣、切中痛點。他的發言常被居民和網民廣傳。 「如果他的屋被燒了，他能否這樣決絕，可以『斷捨離』和道別？ 」「就算你剷平宏福苑，都不能剷走167個街坊、1個消防員，還有千幾戶無家可歸的罪責。」「我期望炳強能用『釘死佢』個態度，去釘死啲問責失職公務員。」 （按：保安局局長鄧炳強回應今年記協換屆選舉時指，如有團體濫用工會名義危害國安，「我一定會釘死你」。） 引來迴響後，謝先生更覺得要珍惜發言機會。今年4月底，大部分居民第一次被集體安排上樓執拾，成為大火後少有聚集大量居民面對記者的機會。他一直認為上樓執拾後，宏福苑居民將不會再聚在一起，再難公開面對傳媒發聲，他要為街坊說平時不敢說的話。平日緊貼時事的他，說話的靈感取自政府官員處理大火的措辭﹐「我就直接入中路㗎啦。」 拿捏內心的怒火是謝先生的課題。「沒有憤怒我也不會說，公正和公義也是我的核心和前提。」身為基督徒，謝先生覺得是上帝讓他遇到這場災難，受訪也是回應上帝的呼召。 本職工程界的他，眼見香港地盤天秤倒塌、瑪麗醫院𨋢槽歪斜，接二連三的工程意外，讓他一直對發生下一場災難有心理準備。當親歷火場並逃生出來時，看到烈火燒毀宏福苑，他固然為之震撼。但當他現在回想，他對悲劇的發生並不感到特別驚訝。 不過，即使他居住的單位完好無缺，這一年，他仍目睹許多後續的痛苦。他看著老街坊為了安家，七八十歲低頭研讀售樓書。有街坊災後情緒飽受困擾、需要會見精神科，來問他自己到底應否賣樓，他無法為街坊作決定，只能誠實為對方分析局勢。 「燒了第二個人的屋企，我都覺得是我的屋企。」他說。 平日緊貼時事的謝先生，說話的靈感取自政府官員處理大火的措辭。攝：林振東/端傳媒 絕望中，謝先生思考自己能做什麼。他自小在廣福邨長大，成年後再和妻兒搬到相鄰的宏福苑，對大埔感情深厚。有社區組織在大埔辦二手市集支持災民，他就到處貼海報，希望讓區內居民知道自己能參與、能支援宏福苑的街坊。好幾個星期日，他在二手市集向受災街坊派超市現金券和月餅，給小朋友派玩具。 他慶幸自己身處其中，有能力去幫忙，和街坊同渡這劫難。「我說可幸的意思是，我能參與其中，我寧願受災那個是我，而不想是其他人。」 謝先生說話的時候總是伴隨著爽朗的笑聲，彷彿在災難面前，除了笑，別無他法。「你也沒辦法。大家當笑話笑，係咁㗎咋。」 對他來說，現世有種種限制，宗教是他內心祈盼的出路。「人的層面是得個吉，或者在今世的層面是得個吉（落得一場空）。」但在基督教信仰裡，末世大審判時上帝會裁決善惡，「大審判時就會算帳，所有隱藏的（罪）也會浮現出來。」 他想繼續留在香港，「去英國好，還是去澳洲好，或是紐西蘭好些，抑或是留在香港好？你永遠沒法這樣去秤。那邊也有那邊的不好，烏克蘭也還有人在生存。」他和相熟的街坊說，無論他們決定賣樓與否，他也會繼續與大家同行。 他覺得，既然他能夠捱過大火一役，那麼他也更能夠在鉅變中生存下去。 「珍惜這段時間去說話」 一年後，許太還是會阻止家人看宏福苑的新聞。她7歲的孫問她：「爺爺嫲嫲搬去新家，會否像之前那樣火燭？」 她回想，包括她在內的居民從大維修工程開始不斷投訴，卻沒有人理會，「如果肉緊一點，不會發生。」大火發生後，居民已經沒法再爭拗什麼，「大家都無得郁。無得郁了。」 但她說他們還是得生活，「我70歲人也沒有那個氣力、精神，與他們慢慢磨。」 大火週年前兩日，港聯辦以「港澳平」署名發文指港府決意「刮骨療傷」，以系統性改革破除頑疾。文中又稱，要對各種「以災亂港的圖謀保持警惕」，在中央支持下，港府定能帶領社會，譜寫「由治及興」的新篇章。同日，政府宣布動用捐款發放兩項「新生活支持補助」——向宏福苑業主派發30萬港元；每名死者家屬獲發放20萬港元。 不少遺屬在週年接受訪問。他們繼續追討和問責，並希望政府每年舉辦官方悼念活動，在宏福苑建一個紀念碑。早前，政府已宣布不會辦官方悼念，並強調「絕對允許合法悼念」，著市民小心選擇悼念活動。 歐太坐在來往策誠軒的穿梭巴士上，途經宏福苑。攝：鄧家烜/端傳媒 一個晚上，歐太獨個坐在廣福休憩處，看著夜裡的宏福苑，跟記者講電話。 歐太說，自己以前專注家庭，少看新聞，沒理政治。這一年，她變成了少數的人。「生活平淡時，當然覺得所有事都沒問題，只需要（專注）局限於家裡就夠。但是當發生了這麼大的事，迫我要去看家以外的事，要看香港的事。」 居民的心底常常懼怕宏福苑很快會就被遺忘。「1126這個重要日子前會有關注，所以我們要說自己的想法。之後傳媒、香港市民和我們都要休息，所以要很珍惜這段時間去說話。可能再下次，香港市民關心宏福苑就已經是立法（收購業權）的時候了。」 她不確定大火一年當天將會發生什麼事情。「我們大家都不敢說約在一起回去，」她說，「但緊張宏福、喜歡宏福的宏福人，那天怎樣也會回來。」 「多謝你陪我聊了這麼久。」她一再重覆道謝。「聽我們這麼長的心聲。」 （尊重受訪者意願，許太、Mike 為化名。） 宏福苑大火一年 華文世界不可或缺的深度報導和多元聲音

content:
美国贸易代表办公室就与制造业结构性产能过剩和生产相关的 14 项 301 条款调查做出决定并建议采取行动 2026 年 11 月 25 日星期三 - 06:19 华盛顿 — 今天，美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔 (Jamieson Greer) 根据 1974 年《贸易法》第 301 条确定 14 个经济体与结构性过剩产能和生产相关的行为、政策和做法制造业的过剩产能和生产是不合理的，会给美国商业带来负担或限制，因此可以根据《贸易法》第 301(b) 条提起诉讼。美国贸易代表办公室（USTR）也发布了支持这些决定的具体经济报告。今天的决定涵盖的 14 个经济体是中国、欧盟、新加坡、瑞士、印度尼西亚、马来西亚、柬埔寨、泰国、韩国、越南、台湾、孟加拉国、日本和印度。贸易代表目前尚未就墨西哥或挪威做出决定。格里尔大使表示：“几十年来，我们的许多贸易伙伴采取了针对制造业、工资和劳动力抑制、金融和其他支持、非市场经济投入以及其他市场扭曲做法的产业战略，这些做法使贸易平衡向有利于他们的方向倾斜，同时侵蚀了美国的制造业基础。”
“认识到这一点，自2016年以来，从唐纳德·特朗普、乔·拜登、习近平到埃马纽埃尔·马克龙等领导人都认识到结构性产能和生产过剩对全球经济构成的威胁。但是，在七国集团、二十国集团、世贸组织和其他论坛上的连续声明没有带来变化的情况下，特朗普总统提议采取行动，消除这些不公平的行为、政策和做法。通过这样做，我们可以为美国工人创造公平的竞争环境，并制定一个新的、更世界经济的可持续发展之路。”  对于以下 14 个经济体，美国贸易代表已确定某些造成、维持或导致结构性产能和生产过剩的行为、政策和做法是不合理的，会给美国商业带来负担或限制。孟加拉国：孟加拉国的不合理行为、政策和做法包括（1）维持和扩大其制造业，特别是关键部门的工业计划； (2) 生产激励措施，促进生产和出口； （三）劳动保护不完善的； （4）金融抑制政策； (5) 未能解决全球产能和生产过剩问题，包括通过来自非市场经济体的进口和外国直接投资。这些法案、政策和做法通过以下方式给美国商业带来负担或限制：(1) 减少美国生产商和出口商在孟加拉国和第三国市场的商业机会； （二）损害美国利益
导致美国制造业的生产、出口、就业和投资损失； (3) 增加美国经济安全风险，包括对 NME 投入的依赖。在成衣和服装领域尤其如此。请在此处阅读美国贸易代表办公室的报告。柬埔寨：柬埔寨的不合理行为、政策和做法包括（1）产业政策规定了明确的出口和制造目标，而不是基于市场原则； (2) 吸收或扩大外国制造能力，特别是非市场经济国家制造能力的投资激励措施； （三）全球产能过剩问题未能解决
